clauses.text:
Executive Order 12182 of December 14, 1979
Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute  
Between the Long Island Rail Road and Certain of its Em­
ployees
A dispute exists between The Long Island Rail Road and certain of its 
employees represented by Participating Labor Organizations designated in list 
attached hereto and made a part hereof.
This dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the 
Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
This dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, threatens 
substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a 
section of the country of essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 10 of the 
Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it is hereby ordered as 
follows:
1-101. Establishm ent o f Board. There is established a board of three members 
to be appointed by the President to investigate this dispute. No member of the 
board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of 
railroad employees or any carrier.
1-102. Report. The board shall report its finding to the President with respect 
to the dispute within 30 days from the date of this Order.
1-103. M aintaining Conditions. As provided by Section 10 of the Railway 
Labor Act, as amended, from this date and for 30 days after the board has 
made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by The Long Island Rail Road, or by its employees, in the conditions out 
of which the dispute arose.

reported_material_gaps: Actual completion of the EO12182 board investigation and actual report to the President have not been established. Section1-102 imposes a30-day reporting deadline only. The report deadline is not proof of performance or a first-end date.

Section1-103 independently maintains the disputed conditions until30days after the board actually reports, with an express agreement exception. The missing actual report date and any relevant agreement/settlement defining earlier permitted changes leave its first end and substantive residual effects unresolved. Section10 of the Railway Labor Act (45USC160), expressly invoked for this rule, has not been read in a held historical statutory text. No whole_order_end is asserted.
versions.research_rationale: This partial candidate retains provisional NO. The complete official EO12182 extract includes its three numbered sections and an expressly incorporated list of seven labor organizations. Six exact spans preserve the party-scope incorporation, board establishment, member-disqualification rule, reporting duty, continuing no-change rule, and attached list; signature/editorial furniture is excluded from operative quotations. The held PDF hash matches GPO fixity and there is no material text or completeness ambiguity; page images were not inspected. Full EO12379 section7 immediately revokes EO12182, without deferred effective wording elsewhere in that actor; August17,1982 is recorded only as a later formal revocation event. Section1-103 is a concrete earlier-ending mechanism dependent on actual report plus30days and an agreement exception, and remains distinct from section1-102 reporting deadline. Since the actual report and relevant agreement history are not established, no first-end or whole-order date is inferred. Bounded later-number/regulatory searches and explicit rejection of cross-actor machine contamination do not supply those occurrence facts.

reasons: The complete original comprises three numbered provisions, four distinct commands, and the expressly incorporated seven-organization party scope. The candidate six spans retain incorporation, establishment, disqualification, report, no-change command and annex without omitting a participating union.

Six original quote spans, their six duplicate source quoted_text fields and six actor quoted_text occurrences exactly match held source text. Text SHA256 values match actual files. Original and actor GPO fixity records were inspected and match.

The complete EO12379 section 7 expressly revokes this order. The signature is August 17, 1982; no deferred effective clause or target saving occurs in the full actor. The candidate keeps that event separate from first_end.

Section 1-102 is a 30-day report deadline. Section 1-103 runs through 30 days after an actual report, with an agreement exception. The candidate correctly leaves each first_end and whole_order_end null and preserves the occurrence gap.

The incorporated party scope and annex are legal scope components, not independent commands to the unions. Terminated describes their operation as part of this EO; it does not assert that any listed organization ceased to exist.

All post-original Long Island held EO matches were independently read in full under METHOD_STOP_01. These establish separate section 9A boards and periods. The later explicit report/termination recitals identify EO12874, EO13654 or EO14349, not EO12182. They neither supply an actual 1979 report nor revive the old order.

The express Railway Labor Act section 10 historical-text gap is material to independently statutory effects and remains in the candidate. The asserted terminated states are upheld for the EO-derived commands only.

Bounded later-source entries accurately state numeric/regulatory coverage and producer triage limits. Independent review adds full named-source reads; neither record proves universal absence of other legal events.
